verdict.tagline: Brutal tactical battles buried under steep queues and technical friction.
for_you_if: you thrive on hardcore tactical squad communication
you can endure harsh initial learning curves
you enjoy large scale strategic warfare
not_for_you_if: you experience persistent crashes and connection errors
you lack patience for long server queues
you dislike sudden deaths from unseen enemies

distortion_flags.sentence: Player sentiment grows more positive the longer they spend with the game.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: New players face severe connection errors, technical instability, and strict community barriers.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience long wait times, full servers, and lengthy queues when attempting to join matches.

citations.review_text: I was excited to try this game but was disappointed with what I found.  HORRENDOUSLY long load times, I think it even got stuck on an infinite load screen once, the game is online only so no offline play or single player mode which is a problem because most of the servers of full and no room to join so not only are you waiting on ridiculous long load times but you're waiting on ridiculous long que times too!  Even if you try a server that claims to be only half full you'll discover that there's only 5 or 6 player actually playing so you're stuck running around bored!

after an hour and half on the game, most of that time was waiting for a slot in a server. you cant play as solo. you have to be in a squad  with someone in charge, usually on a power trip. the game has deffo got potential and needs to be a bit more friendly for new players. i got booted off a server twice because i didnt know what i was doing really regarding all the different things you have to learn. some of these players who can spend their life on a game needs to understand its supposed to be fun and stop taking it so serious . its a game. chill out.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the lack of a proper tutorial or offline single-player mode for learning the game.

citations.review_text: Dropped in three servers to full squads and roamed around alone until i got killed from 300 meters away. No tutorial or community engagement whatsoever.

overhyped, overrated. the game is unwelcoming to new players. its clunky, junky and filled with try-hards that will kick you from the server or request it and EVERYONE will immediately vote yes. tutorial is just yourself in the map, hands on your dick. no pve crash course to get your bearings, no learning curve, spawn camping, die and redeploy, rinse and repeat.

Honestly, it has something great going for it, and I can for sure see the interest in it, but it just might not be for me. I have some nitpicks, but maybe it's just me. Game is pretty boring, and when you are able to even get close to an objective, or area that's even near anything someone will snipe you, get blown up, or something. I get this is suppose to be a gritty WWII shooter, but it's pretty boring. Tutorials don't really help at all, and there's no help in the community.

claims.claim: Movement mechanics are described as slow, and players encounter environmental navigation issues such as being unable to climb through windows or getting stuck on terrain objects.

citations.review_text:
I have no idea how this went from "mixed" to "very positive".bit should have stayed mixed...
 I downloaded it solely because it changed and thought maybe they fixed whatever was wrong with it at launch.
 I was in game roughly 40 minutes. I ran in snow for most of it. Just running. No enemies, nothing but twigs and snow and a few allies. Running was like a snail pace with a diaper on.  Tried to climb through a window but you can't. Then I somehow was able to vault over a fence my height with ease. I died 3 times before seeing my first enemy. There were 2 specks 100 meters away, finally.  The rifle has no scope so all I could do is sit there in cover. Then I waited. And waited. And waited. Then I eventually died from I assume a sniper shot. That's as far as I needed to go with this. Horrible graphics. Combat is way too slow, clunky af, and just boring.  Waste of time.

THE WORST WW2 SHOOTER IVE EVER PLAYED!!!!!! The game is janky buggy unoptimized trash! I was crawling in a forest under suppressive fire and got glued to a tree i was barely touching. No way to get unstuck. Players in chat said it was "user error". Some maps you get 120 fps and other maps youre lucky to get a stable 50. Game feels terrible to play and the gameplay is nonexistent. You run entrench yourself and constantly die to people you cant see in one shot. But if you shoot others they seem to take 2 or 3 shots from a rifle before going down. Super annoying to play and really a terrible experience i wouldn't recommend to anyone but the hardcore nerds who have all the time in the world and no life.

claims.claim: New players report a lack of communication or voice chat usage among teammates on servers.

citations.review_text: The game is fun, but the whole reason of the game is to win and collaborate with your team, right? NOT A SINGLE PERSON TALKED ON ANY SERVER! The game is ok if you want to die under a minute or two, but I was hoping to hear someone having fun or be dramatic when they get shot by a enemy player.

i thought "oh, maybe this game isnt as bad as people say, maybe theyre just bad"
im uninstalling. dogshit graphics, poor performance, admins suck, full of teamkillers, spawn camping is rampant, the sounds arent even properly lined up, so dont try to find that guy shooting at you, just accept your fate. there is 0 fun to really be found here. no ones in the chats. a huge waste of money and time. i hate this so much. these devs have never used a gun, nor have they ever heard one be fired. if they have, then they put in 0 effort. im going to try to get a refund. i thought id have fun with my husband, i did not. im going over to battlefield, its somehow more realistic than this.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that community servers enforce strict requirements such as mandatory microphone use or level caps, and players face kicking or bans for being new or uncommunicative.

citations.review_text: This game is kinda shit ngl. First spawned in and had no idea what was going on or where I was supposed to go. Got sniped from idek where. Tried to spawn on the objective where all the other players are, but it won't let you because apparently the objective is being attacked. Gee, I fucking wonder why. Then I realized that most community servers require you to have a mic to play. fuck that. Immediately closed the game. If you're trying to play casually without worrying about voice chat, please, get ANYTHING else but this shit.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

First server: Joined Soviets, did absolutely nothing, somehow won the battle, then got kicked for being under level 20.

Second server: Same shit. Kicked again.

Third server: Joined Soviets as MG. Asked a random guy, “Sir, when’s my training?” He told me to run across a field.

I ran. I survived. He said, “You just saved the day.”

Then my squad got wiped, I followed PizzaGuy, and a German MG turned me into Swiss cheese.

Switched to Germany as Medic, saved two guys, and somehow won the battle.

0 kills. 2 revives. 100% confused. 10/10, would absolutely run across that field again.

after an hour and half on the game, most of that time was waiting for a slot in a server. you cant play as solo. you have to be in a squad  with someone in charge, usually on a power trip. the game has deffo got potential and needs to be a bit more friendly for new players. i got booted off a server twice because i didnt know what i was doing really regarding all the different things you have to learn. some of these players who can spend their life on a game needs to understand its supposed to be fun and stop taking it so serious . its a game. chill out.

Beautiful maps and game mechanics but very Toxic community, you get kicked out for being new even on ''new player servers'' run around and get killed rinse and repeat. Great game if youre jobless and dont offer anything to society because you will have all 24 hours of the day dedicated to learn everything in it. This game is not for new players.
if your new to the game or dont have a microphone, or dont speak german, dont bother.

overhyped, overrated. the game is unwelcoming to new players. its clunky, junky and filled with try-hards that will kick you from the server or request it and EVERYONE will immediately vote yes. tutorial is just yourself in the map, hands on your dick. no pve crash course to get your bearings, no learning curve, spawn camping, die and redeploy, rinse and repeat.

claims.claim: Players encounter frequent connection errors, crashes on startup, and perpetual loading screens preventing them from entering matches.

citations.review_text: Completely unplayable, constant crashes. My entire one hour of playtime has been spent in loading screens trying to get into a lobby. Not worth the time or money wasted on it. About to refund

Loaded game. Crashed on start up.
Loaded game again, black screen after "press button to continue".
Loaded again, made it to server screen. Dared to click a button while searching for server. Crashed.
Loaded again. Got into the server screen. Selected a server. 6 minute of waiting. Closed game.
Loaded again. Tried loading into server again. 5 minutes later nothing, still loading. Closed game.
Waiting for my refund to be accepted.
GG

"Lost Connection To Host" Cannot join any server. Tried every fix suggested. NOTHING.

Give me my money back

claims.claim: Performance is reported as poor with stutters, hitching, and low frame rates despite adjusting settings.

citations.review_text: truly abysmal performance even on lowest settings and with optimizations. Servers are also very few and crowded.
Very inconsitent performance. Even on my high end pc I have extreme stuttering. I tried everything from reddit but nothing worked.

Final edit: game refunded. While I appreciate the devs replying, the fact of the matter is these issues have existed for years, and replying to reviews for the publicity =/= fixing the game over the last several years. You had your chance. You lost it. I don't have time to spend money on a game and then troubleshoot it for hours for it to maybe work, while the refund timer expires.

Edit: finally got in and no matter what I do, the game stutters and runs terribly. Lower settings, same problem. Different servers. Restart machine. Garbage optimization that causes stutters and hitching resulting in losing gunfights and losing immersion. Refund request is already in

"Lost Connection to Host" perpetual error this many years down the line, still not addressed. Will be refunding if it doesn't start working. 0.6 hours of sitting in a damn menu

claims.claim: The game features performance issues including frame rate drops and stuttering.

citations.review_text:
I really wanted to like this game, but the optimization is an absolute joke. 
Running this on a current gen gaming rig at 1440p gives terrible framerates and constant stutters. 
On top of that, bushes and trees look terrible at range... just a blurry mush that makes it impossible to spot enemies before they shoot you.

 Great concept, but completely ruined by poor technical execution.

Game is a complete and utter shit show. The FPS stability is an absolute nightmare in this game one second its 200+ then the next second it drops to 100 something its just up and down. Getting into a game is also annoying not all servers speak the language you speak, most of them are full, the ones that are like 90 something players aren't full but for some reason they make you weight in a queue despite not being full. It's either the server is full or not enough players and/or the ping is way above 100. Can't find a well populated server or one with decent ping less than 100. If it has good ping its an empty server, if the server has a lot of players it has high ping, its never populated enough with decent ping its always one or the other. Then don't get me started on some of the dumbass rules different servers have like not being allowed to do certain things below a certain level and getting kicked/killed in action by server admins for violating those rules the game just isn't that fun of an experience.
Fun game. Worst performance of any game I've played

citations.review_text:
This game is pretty fun, and in my opinion, I like it better than a lot of WW1 and WW2 first person shooter games out there. There is a good mix of realism and arcade play to make it feel more immersive without making you feel like you just lost everything after you die. My only complaint is the que system. Why is it that only 6 people can be in a que at a time? Why not be like BF1 and make it so much more can que up? I just find that kind of stupid. That's really the only big gripe though. 

Overall, 8/10 game. Really fun.

-Wait an hour to join a server
-Zero logistics on selected team
-Spawn on closest garrison(10 minute walk from frontlines)
-Start walking
-Make it to contested point
-Bullets flying by, no idea where they came from
-Get teamkilled by artillery
Greatest and most realistic game I've ever played. Weirdly easy to fall into.

I'd be lying to say im a hardcore tactical game type of guy, but for me as a new player this game is almost impossible to play. It takes 30 minutes to get into a server without some sort of VIP, then Im subject to getting spawn killed by some vet level 237 player from across the map. The skill curb is just so high and its hard finding anyone in game willing to explain things.

Game is a complete and utter shit show. The FPS stability is an absolute nightmare in this game one second its 200+ then the next second it drops to 100 something its just up and down. Getting into a game is also annoying not all servers speak the language you speak, most of them are full, the ones that are like 90 something players aren't full but for some reason they make you weight in a queue despite not being full. It's either the server is full or not enough players and/or the ping is way above 100. Can't find a well populated server or one with decent ping less than 100. If it has good ping its an empty server, if the server has a lot of players it has high ping, its never populated enough with decent ping its always one or the other. Then don't get me started on some of the dumbass rules different servers have like not being allowed to do certain things below a certain level and getting kicked/killed in action by server admins for violating those rules the game just isn't that fun of an experience.

single_points.text: One reviewer says bushes and trees at range look like a blurry mush that makes it impossible to spot enemies before they shoot you.

citation.review_text:
I really wanted to like this game, but the optimization is an absolute joke. 
Running this on a current gen gaming rig at 1440p gives terrible framerates and constant stutters. 
On top of that, bushes and trees look terrible at range... just a blurry mush that makes it impossible to spot enemies before they shoot you.

 Great concept, but completely ruined by poor technical execution.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that matches and player survival are frequently cut short by being killed instantly from unseen enemies or long-range shots without clear indicators.

citations.review_text:
The primary issue with this game is that for every one thrilling fight where you're laying down fire with a well coordinated team, pushing the enemy, fighting off counter attacks, and actually get to fight someone, there's ten rounds where you're stuck in a squad with no one speaking, you die from an enemy you don't see, and you spend half an hour hearing gunshots while losing objectives. When the mechanics and design principles work in cohesion, it's an amazing experience that blows even the best moments of games like RO2 out of the water. The issue is that those factors rarely play out and you're left with a game that's less exciting on average than a fifteen year old game where most MP matches are five people and a dozen bots. 

It's too late in its lifespan for new players to comfortably jump, the community itself seems to become more and more insulated by the day, you can go matches without hearing someone else speak. The official servers are rough, private servers vary from a genuine blast with cool people all the way to giga hell "NOOOO PLAY BY MY RULES!!!!" Map rotation is poor, with an even poorer distribution of Eastern Front maps, leading to the game getting tedious quickly. Game stability is hit or miss, sometimes not crashing for hours, other times it crashes every 15 minutes. Performance is very hit or miss as well. 

I can't recommend this without severe caveats. If you're looking for something a bit different than Call of Duty or Battlefield, give Red Orchestra 2 a shot first. The active base is small but consistent and you can generally find servers with at least a handful of players, with bots filling out the roster. Enlisted and Easy Red 2 fill somewhat similar niches as RO2, though both are a good bit more casual. If none of those scratch the itch, then I'd say give Hell Let Loose a whirl. Goes on sale for decent prices and there's the occasional free weekend.

Fun mindless game to play but can get very repetive. Works well if youre team is stacked lol. The terrain needs fixing, you get stuck on small 5cent rock in the middle of a gunfight classic, lots of random "open" buildings that dont let you inside. When running past a friendly player, you just spend 30 minutes trying to get past them due to there large figure which is annoying asf. First game ive ever played where the medic class is the least valuable class in the game, everyone rages on about how they get more smoke grenades, yeah mate we're getting rolled for the 7th time, just play as medic and throw smokes allgood. Getting insta killed with headshots is lame, they need to inherit squad incaped state, headshots faster bleedout etc. Die respawn die respawn, your life becomes pretty meaningless if you play medic considering no one else can rev apart from meds lol and no one plays them as much. Lots of random frame drops, sometimes unplayable and requires a reboot which fixes it. Games pretty grindy to unlock other classes which sometimes are essential, i mean its basically 100hrs as rifleman before you can resupply your AT lol. But yeah if you like dying constantly and running from Garrys/OPs and then being shelled by your friendly Arty go for gold, best WW2 slightly milsim experience you can find on the market but not worth the full price imo.
Long runs and getting one shots from hundreds of meters with no kill cam or muzzle flash. It needs a total redesign.

Its not like COD, Red Orcrestra or BF, it's different but so much fun. I only downloaded this after trying HLL Vietnam, and it was cheap. But after 32 hours of playing I'm loving it. Been a team member is important, but you can still be a lone wolf. A micophone is a must and communications with your squad and team is important. 

The graphics are fine and with my setup i'm getting 200fps plus.  There are plenty of servers, and plenty of players. The maps are great, and look really good. It can be frustrating at times getting killed and having no idea where the shot came from, But also you can do the same thing to the opposition . The talk of aimbot hacks is actually true, but I'm still enjoying it. I just wish I had tryed it sooner.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features prolonged travel times across the map to return to objectives, particularly when transport options are lacking.

citations.review_text:
Looks great, sounds great, game is slow, you run for most of the game because nobody does transport, and you run terribly slow, which makes the whole no transport scenario a joke thats just not really worth putting up with. 

Game is well made to a degree, but it has to many sharp edges to really consistantly come back to day to day. 

You wont find squads using tactics like in squad, project reality etc, everyone in this game seems to do mostly their own thing. 

People will sit in a bush all game, kill you and make you run another 15 minutes across the map..... in the end, it gets tiring and boring quick.... Sadly still the best WW2 shooter with tactical elements on a scale smaller than ARMA which makes it more accessable to time restricted people. 

4/10 for me overall when it comes to enjoyment
10/10 for sound design, this game has made me feel like I was in the hedgerows of normandy with my eyes closed 
9.5/10 for graphics, this game is very damn pretty, super beautiful and the effects and particles are the best out of all games to date, watching big bombs explode and kick a 60 - 120 FPS dust cloud into the sky that looks real......... fucking beautiful 

but sadly the game gets a 4/10 when it comes to the little things that just add up too quickly...

Hell Let Loose is a World War II shooter where teamwork is pretty much everything. You can have fun playing solo, but it’s especially entertaining with friends on voice chat. You might start with a plan, but things usually get chaotic pretty quickly. Even when you’re playing alone, random players on proximity chat can make for some hilarious moments.

I enjoy playing all the different roles, and I like that you have to work together instead of just running off on your own. The gunplay feels solid and fairly realistic, although it’s not perfect. For example, there’s no shooting through walls, and the recoil feels pretty mild.

The most annoying part is having to run for ages to get back to the objective, especially when the commander hasn’t built any garrisons. You finally make it to the front and might get taken out straight away. Shooting can also feel laggy in close-quarters combat. Sometimes I land the first shot and still die, which feels unfair.

The graphics are pretty meh, too. For a game from 2021, I expected it to look better compared with other games from around the same time. They’re not terrible, though, and they don’t ruin the game for me.

Overall, Hell Let Loose is a great fit for anyone who likes World War II shooters and cares more about realistic gunplay than impressive graphics. If you’re a bit of a tactics nerd and find games like Call of Duty or Battlefield too arcade-like, HLL could be right up your alley. But if you’re into sprinting around and fast-paced action, it probably isn’t for you.

I unfortunately left a negative recommendation a few days ago based on what I believe might've been solved by either a fault in my amdgpu driver (changing Kernel appears to have helped) or changing my BIOS setting to make my system retrain the DDR5 at every cold boot (which it does quickly anyway), either way it's been running without crashing for the last few days. claims.claim: The game features a steep learning curve and requires reliance on voice chat and team coordination.

citations.review_text:
1,680 hours in.   Absolutely love
Something about the game makes it unique to all WWII FPS. Coordination is key, and a mic is a must if you want to have fun. Look up each class on youtube to get a 5 minute briefing on how to use that class properly. Once you do that you will have endless fun. The game is not as complicated as it seems. If you join a dead squad, just join another that communicates or start your own. it's a great community where you can always ask advice, they want you knowledgeable to help the team.  The majority of the people playing this game know that the only reason it's good is because of communication, so you will definitely find talkers.
absolute banger of a game if you like ww2 games this is for you! its like cod ww2 meets arma reforger 10 out of 10 its a steep learning curve but with a good squad its definitely worth it!!!
Great game requiring teamwork and communication for a good experience. Steep learning curve but a great sense of achievement to be had

The gameplay is really fun. It’s built around teamwork and a command structure that relies on solid coordination.
This is a 50v50 match, but the raw intensity of gunfights and combat isn’t for everyone.
For new and casual players: focus on relaying battlefield intel. Call out tanks, strongpoints, and infantry to your squad leads and command channels. Pass off situations you can’t handle to teammates. Accurate, real-time info is key to winning as a team.

Quick tips for new players looking to jump in: pick engineer and support classes early. Farm resource nodes and drop supplies at the start of the match. This helps you level fast while learning the game mechanics.

This is a team game — you can’t carry the fight alone. Communication is where the real fun lies. Work alongside squad leads and commanders to coordinate your pushes.
Hope everyone grows into a great commander!

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game randomly resets loadout and cosmetic selections when switching between presets.

citation.review_text:
[h1]Great Game, Frustrating Lack of Attention to Longstanding Bugs[/h1]

I genuinely enjoy Hell Let Loose. The atmosphere, large-scale battles, and emphasis on teamwork make it one of the more enjoyable tactical shooters I've played.

However, one of my biggest frustrations is the apparent lack of developer attention to longstanding bugs and basic quality-of-life issues.

The game has been available for over four years, continues to receive updates, and regularly introduces new content. Yet somehow, the developers still haven't managed to properly fix the preset and customization system.

You can spend 30 minutes configuring your loadouts, uniforms, faces, and cosmetics, carefully setting everything up the way you want it, only for the game to randomly reset your selections when switching between presets.

This completely defeats the purpose of having a preset system in the first place.

[h3]How Is This Still an Issue?[/h3]

We're talking about a game that costs around €50, where a relatively basic quality-of-life feature has remained unreliable for years.

I understand that game development is complicated and that bugs aren't always straightforward to fix. However, when a game continues to receive new content while longstanding issues remain unresolved, it raises questions about development priorities.

New maps, cosmetics, and additional content are great, but they shouldn't consistently take precedence over fixing existing systems that players interact with regularly.

What's particularly frustrating is that Hell Let Loose is genuinely a good game underneath these issues. I enjoy the gameplay, and I want to recommend it, but it's difficult to overlook problems that have persisted for this long.

[h3]Final Verdict[/h3]

Hell Let Loose has an excellent foundation, but the developers need to dedicate more attention to polishing and maintaining the systems that are already in the game.
